name: Valley Floodcaller
description:
Flash

You may cast noncreature spells as though they had flash.

Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, Birds, Frogs, Otters, and Rats you control get +1/+1 until end of turn and untap.
assumptions: Node C (`modifier`, `thing: self`, flags `flash`) is read as the creature granting itself the keyword ability "Flash," even though its `to: bf` field sits oddly with a keyword that's normally relevant while the card is castable from hand — there's no better fit among the node roles for "this creature has flash."

Node D (`modifier`, `thing: any`, `cond:grant=flash_cast cond:noncreature`) is read as "You may cast noncreature spells as though they had flash," with `owner: me` restricting it to spells you cast/control.

`thing: bird/frog/otter/rat` on F–M are treated as direct creature-subtype filters ("Birds," "Frogs," "Otters," "Rats") even though the schema notes subtypes normally belong in a `cond:` field rather than in `thing` directly — no coarse type-line word or registry entry fits these four values, so they're taken at face value as the intended subtypes.

Since F–I (all four types' `pt_delta` effects) and J–M (all four types' untap effects) are joined with no `combine` wrapper, all eight fire together as one unconditional bundle (not a modal choice), giving one combined clause rather than four separate per-type sentences.

The order of printed abilities (Flash line, then the cast-as-flash static ability, then the triggered ability) follows the order the nodes are listed/rooted in, since flow doesn't otherwise fix a print order among unrelated roots.
"Untap" (J–M) is treated as an immediate, non-durational part of the same effect sentence as the +1/+1 boost, since only F–I carry `lifetime:turn`.
couldNotDerive: Whether the four subtype effects are meant to print as one combined sentence ("Birds, Frogs, Otters, and Rats...") or as separate clauses/sentences per type — the flow only shows four parallel edges, not a preferred surface wording.
Whether "noncreature spell(s)" in the triggered/static abilities is meant to include all noncreature card types uniformly or is otherwise scoped — only the bare `cond:noncreature` flag is given.
Rarity — explicitly withheld from the self registry.
Any supertype (e.g., Legendary) — not present in the self registry's type line, so omitted rather than guessed.
Reminder text, if any, for the granted "cast as though it had flash" ability.
notes:
Real card confirmed via forge-model/data/valley-floodcaller.txt: {2}{U} Creature — Otter Wizard, 2/2. Oracle: "Flash\nYou may cast noncreature spells as though they had flash.\nWhenever you cast a noncreature spell, Birds, Frogs, Otters, and Rats you control get +1/+1 until end of turn. Untap them."

This is the 3rd exam attempt, run after a real translator fix expanding the untap effect's node(s) from Bird-only to all four creature types (Bird/Frog/Otter/Rat), matching Forge's shared ValidCards$ Bird.YouCtrl,Frog.YouCtrl,Otter.YouCtrl,Rat.YouCtrl list used by both the PumpAll and chained UntapAll sub-effects. The packet now carries J/K/L/M as four parallel untap nodes (bird/frog/otter/rat) mirroring F/G/H/I's own four parallel pump nodes, closing the exact gap attempt 2 flagged (node J previously named only "bird", leaving Frog/Otter/Rat un-untapped in the decomposition even though Forge's SubAbility$ shared the identical multi-type ValidCards$ string).

The examiner's blind reconstruction is a full match: mana cost, type line, P/T (via self registry), Flash, the flash-granting static ability, and the combined pump+untap trigger across all four subtypes are all present and correctly scoped (no target flag correctly read as an unrestricted "each Bird/Frog/Otter/Rat you control" effect, not a chosen target). The only textual difference from Scryfall's oracle wording is where the sentence break falls ("get +1/+1 until end of turn and untap" vs "get +1/+1 until end of turn. Untap them.") — a phrasing choice with identical rules meaning, not a mechanical gap, consistent with the process's match criterion ("wording doesn't need to match Scryfall's exact phrasing, only meaning"). No decomposition gaps, schema gaps, or misinterpretations found. This closes out the valley-floodcaller exam.
